Your code runs without errors, but the output is different from what you expected. Thankfully, Copilot can help debug your code in both situations. To learn how, work through the following examples. pages.text: Leave Benefits | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Leave Benefits More in This Section Close Family and Medical Leave (FMLA) Funeral Leave Government Contracts Holidays Jury Duty Personal Leave Sick Leave Vacations Many companies offer leave benefits that allow employees to take time off from work for various reasons. Leave benefits – whether paid, unpaid or partially paid – are generally an agreement between the employer and employee, or employees representative (such as a union). Family and Medical Leave Act The Family and Medical Leave Act provides certain employees with up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year. It also requires that their group health benefits be maintained during the leave. Fair Labor Standards Act While certain types of leave are required by law, other types are voluntary incentives provided by employers. There is a common misconception that Department of Labor regulates leave benefits through the Fair Labor Standards Act . But, the FLSA only covers certain types of leave. In fact, there are a number of employment practices which FLSA does not regulate. For example, it does not require: Vacation, holiday, severance, or sick pay Meal or rest periods, holidays off, or vacations Premium pay for weekend or holiday work Pay raises or fringe benefits Discharge notice, reason for discharge, or immediate payment of final wages to terminated employees Statistics The Employee Benefits Survey of the Bureau of Labor Statistics covers the incidence and characteristics of employee benefits.

pages.description: Scientists need postmortem human brains for research, but general organ donation programs don’t harvest them. Tish Hevel found a solution.
pages.text: Leaving your brain to science: don’t let myths dissuade you | National Geographic This donated brain of a 101-year-old man is larger than a typical brain of someone his age. He’s said to have been astute until the day he died. Photograph By Rebecca Hale Premium MAGAZINE Leaving your brain to science: don’t let myths dissuade you Scientists need postmortem human brains for research, but general organ donation programs don’t harvest them. Tish Hevel found a solution. By Lori Cuthbert 3 min read This story appears in the October 2018 issue of National Geographic magazine. Brains are in short supply. Neuroscientists need brain tissue of all types to study the diseases that affect more than 15 percent of people in the world. Enter Tish Hevel. In 2015, after Hevel’s father died from Lewy body dementia, her family wanted to offer his brain for research—but knew that it would take much more than an organ donor card. The experience inspired Hevel to create the Brain Donor Project “to raise awareness of the critical need” and make enrolling easier for would-be donors. Nearly two years in, more than 2,000 people have signed up. 3:43 Busting myths about donating your brain The organization that Tish Hevel created—online at braindonorproject.org —aims to simplify “the process of donating postmortem human brains for research,” she says, and dispel misconceptions about it. Legal Authorities for Isolation and Quarantine For Everyone May 15, 2024 At a glance Federal regulations allow staff at U.S. Port Health Stations to take certain actions to limit the introduction and spread of communicable diseases in the United States. These stations, located at major U.S. ports of entry, serve as focal points for responses to infections in travelers that could lead to outbreaks in destination communities. Isolation and Quarantine Isolation and quarantine help protect the public by preventing exposure to people who have or may have a contagious disease. Isolation separates sick people with a quarantinable communicable disease from people who are not sick. Quarantine separates and restricts the movement of people who were exposed to a contagious disease to see if they become sick. In addition to serving as health functions, isolation and quarantine also are "police power" functions, derived from the right of the state to take action affecting individuals for the benefit of society. Legend guide # This legend guide extends the legend docstring - please read it before proceeding with this guide. This guide makes use of some common terms, which are documented here for clarity: legend entry # A legend is made up of one or more legend entries. An entry is made up of exactly one key and one label. legend key # The colored/patterned marker to the left of each legend label. legend label # The text which describes the handle represented by the key. legend handle # The original object which is used to generate an appropriate entry in the legend. Controlling the legend entries # Calling legend() with no arguments automatically fetches the legend handles and their associated labels. Credit: M. King/NIST Torque wrenches — and the people who use them to build and maintain planes — are unsung heroes of the skies. Torque wrenches measure the force that causes an object to rotate. Aircraft mechanics use torque wrenches to ensure that bolts and fasteners on planes are correctly tightened. Without them, a plane could come apart midflight. But like any measurement tool, torque wrenches need to be calibrated regularly to make sure they’re giving accurate readings. If these measurements are off, the results could be disastrous. BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the League One side at the start of the 2024-25 season - named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month . The online gambling company posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin." The club, which had faced criticism from fans' group The Foxes Trust, said it had reached a "mutual agreement" to end its partnership with the firm, and supporters who had bought shirts in the past 28 days could exchange them. Announcing the club's partnership in 2024, Leicester City said BC Game - which is not available to users in the UK - was a "socially responsible platform" and aimed to provide an "enjoyable and safe gaming experience". When Elfie was confirmed as BC Game's brand ambassador, the firm - in a post on LinkedIn on 3 November - said she had an "established presence in gaming communities". pages.text: Leicestershire heart surgery survivor, 11, wins national karting crown at Silverstone Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Triple heart surgery survivor, 11, wins karting crown 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Rob Sissons , East Midlands health correspondent and Sam French , Leicester Stu Stretton Photography Daniel hopes to stay involved in the sport in the future and has recently started coaching other children A boy who underwent three open-heart operations has urged other children to "follow their dreams" after he was crowned a national karting champion. Daniel, 11, was born with a complex heart condition that saw him spend the first six months of his life in and out of hospital. Despite his condition, Daniel remained active and took up karting when he was four, culminating in his national championship win this year. After picking up his trophy at Silverstone on Saturday, Daniel said: "Follow your dreams and don't give up." Stu Stretton Photography Daniel hopes his achievement will inspire other children facing challenges to follow their dreams Daniel's father, Krisztian, said it felt like a "bad dream" when his son became seriously ill at three days old. pages.text: Lelio Orsi (about 1511 - 1587) | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Lelio Orsi is recorded as a painter in Reggio in northern Italy in 1536 and 1544. In 1553-4 he visited Venice and Rome, and after 1559 he was in Novellara. There are no contemporary records of his paintings, and no signed works, except one drawing. A group of small religious paintings, all by the same hand, are attributed to him. They show the influence of Michelangelo and Correggio . The inscription on his grave at Novellara (written by his son) says that he was great in architecture and painting, but greatest as a draughtsman. Some of the drawings attributed to him bear this out. pages.text: Lelio Orsi | The Walk to Emmaus | NG1466 | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Lelio Orsi, 'The Walk to Emmaus', about 1565-75 The Walk to Emmaus Lelio Orsi Room 6 About the work Overview In-depth Overview The Gospel of Luke tells how after the Crucifixion, Cleopas and another of Christ’s disciples set out from Jerusalem for the village of Emmaus. They were joined by a stranger who recounted the prophecies concerning the Messiah’s death and resurrection. It was not until the three ate together later at an inn in Emmaus that the disciples recognised the risen Christ (Luke 24: 13–29). Lelio Orsi sets the episode on an overcast evening – bursts of light break through black clouds, casting a supernatural glow. One disciple clasps his belt while the other wrings his hands in anguish as Christ in the centre explains the prophecies. The small goldfinch in the bottom right-hand corner is a common symbol of the Passion (Christ’s torture and crucifixion). The painting, which probably dates to about 1565–75, reveals Orsi’s interest in the work of Michelangelo, which he would have seen on an earlier trip to Rome. pages.title: Leonardo's horse took 500 years to make | National Geographic
pages.description: Da Vinci died before he could complete his massive bronze sculpture of a horse, something that wouldn’t occur until the 20th century
pages.text: Leonardo's horse took 500 years to make | National Geographic Published April 30, 2019 • 2 min read Studies of horses drawn by Leonardo da Vinci circa 1490, when he was planning “Il Gran Cavallo.” Collection of the Royal Library, Windsor Castle, Windsor, England Photograph by Print Collector/Album At the request of Ludovico Sforza, the future Duke of Milan , Leonardo da Vinci began working on a sculpture that would be the largest equestrian statue in the world in 1482. Leonardo made sketches of the horses in the Sforza stables, from which he designed a 24-foot-high clay model. Leonardo wanted to cast the horse in a single operation and designed elaborate plaster molds to make that possible. In his innovative process, the inverted molds would be buried between two ovens, and molten bronze would fill them to cast the statue. War versus art The plans were set to create the giant horse, but war with France engulfed Milan in 1499. Sforza needed the bronze for weapons, not art, and the materials were diverted to forge cannons. The French defeated Milan, occupied Sforza's lands, and destroyed the clay horse. Leonardo ’s drawings and plans survived, but the artist died in May 1519 before “Il Gran Cavallo” could be brought to life. Gift horse Roughly five hundred years later, inspired by a 1977 National Geographic article, “The Horse That Never Was,” American art patron Charles C. Dent made it his life’s work to erect the statue. pages.text: Les Hôtes du Louvre - Kader Attia et Elizabeth Peyton Les Hôtes du Louvre - Kader Attia et Elizabeth Peyton Aller au contenu Les Hôtes du Louvre Kader Attia et Elizabeth Peyton En cours Artistes invités 24 septembre – 14 décembre 2026 following sections sections précédentes Les Hôtes du Louvre Kader Attia et Elizabeth Peyton 24 septembre – 14 décembre 2026 Informations générales Durée moyenne 30 MIN Lieu Aile Sully - Salle de la Chapelle Langue(s) Français, Anglais Tarif (musée + exposition) Compris dans la réservation du billet d’entrée au musée Consulter les tarifs Réserver un billet Partager cet article De 2024 à l'été 2026, Kader Attia et Elizabeth Peyton sont les Hôtes du Louvre. Kader Attia (né en 1970 à Dugny, vit et travaille à Paris et à Berlin) est connu pour son œuvre à la frontière des formes et des réflexions, entre enquête sensible et pensée contemporaine. Elizabeth Peyton (née en 1965 dans le Connecticut, vit et travaille à Paris et à New York) fait vibrer la peinture au travers de l'art du portrait. Pendant deux ans, ils ont habité les espaces physiques et imaginaires du Louvre. Ils y ont eu un atelier, y ont créé, ont conversé avec ses équipes, ont fait partie de ses publics. Voisins par leurs ateliers, ils partagent désormais l'espace d'exposition de la salle de la Chapelle pour donner à voir le résultat de leurs parcours respectifs au musée : le film et l'installation dans le cas de Kader Attia sont inspirés de sa propre fréquentation intime de l'institution, contemplant la fluctuation des époques, des mémoires et des regards, faisant du regard un objet.

Depuis lors, le Louvre se montre généreux à travers ses prêts, ses dépôts, ses expositions ou des partenariats afin d’aider des musées territoriaux à compléter des fonds, à proposer des expositions temporaires ou à renouveler leur programme muséographique. Il y a aujourd’hui presque autant d’œuvres du Louvre exposées dans les murs du Palais à Paris (environ 35 000) que dans les musées de région. Le Louvre se place ainsi au service de tous les territoires et musées de France Politique de dépôts Le Louvre est plus que tout autre musée ancré dans l’ensemble du territoire français à travers une politique de dépôts successifs et continus depuis le 19è siècle auprès des musées de France. Les partenaires historiques, liés au Louvre depuis les envois du 19e siècle, restent bien sûr des partenaires essentiels, de même que des institutions comme le Petit Palais d’Avignon et le musée Bonnat dont les collections sont liées étroitement au Louvre, mais il s’est positionné depuis quelques années au service de tous les territoires, et renforce sa position de partenaire privilégié des musées de France dans ses domaines de compétences. Plus de 150 millions de vies ont été sauvées grâce à la vaccination au cours des 50 dernières années. The event bring together artists and curators who engage with notions of 'spiral’ time, as theorised by Brazilian scholar Leda Maria Martins. Through presentations by María Magdalena Campos-Pons, Daniel Lind-Ramos, Nádia Taquary, Julieta Gonzalez, Claire Tancons and Thiago de Paula Souza, it examines how Afro-diasporic cosmologies, traditions and non-linear time inform artistic and curatorial practices. pages.text: Lessons of the Hour | Perth Museum Explore Isaac Julien's acclaimed film portrait of Frederick Douglass at Perth Museum Perth Museum is the first and only Scottish venue on this new ARTIST ROOMS tour of Isaac Julien’s (b.1960) immersive film installation Lessons of the Hour - Frederick Douglass 2019 . This exhibition brings Julien’s poetic meditation on the life and legacy of Frederick Douglass into dialogue with the histories of abolition, slavery and racial justice in Perthshire and across Scotland. Born into slavery in Maryland in 1818, Douglass became a pioneering abolitionist, writer and intellectual, playing a critical role in anti-slavery and human rights movements in the US, Britain and beyond. During his 1846 campaign against slavery across the UK and Ireland, Douglass delivered four speeches in Perth in the former City Hall building, on the very site where Perth Museum now stands. Julien’s work, and in turn this exhibition, takes its title from Douglass’ final delivered speech in 1894. About Perth Museum Perth Museum is a landmark cultural destination in Perthshire, home to the Stone of Destiny and a dynamic programme of exhibitions exploring Scotland’s history, culture and contemporary life. Since opening, it has welcomed more than 500,000 visitors and was the only Scottish finalist for Art Fund Museum of the Year 2025. Photo by Joe Furgal, Ralph Rinzler Folklife Archives A common idiom in American English casts the circus in an unfavorable light: “It’s a circus over there!” tends to mean something messy and chaotic. Yet if you look at the inner workings of an actual circus, the level of skill, coordination, and execution necessary for such a production is immeasurable. The split-second timing of a flying trapeze catch, the unspoken understanding and total trust between acrobats as they tower atop each other, the quick-wittedness of a clown as they turn an unscripted interaction into a highlight of the show—these performances require lifetimes of training, the strictest schedules, and the perfectly coordinated efforts of teams both in the spotlight and in the wings. Engagement rates, like open rates and click-through rates , are important metrics and tracking them can tell you how engaged and interested your audience is in your content.
